title: The first description of CTNNB1 syndrome in the Tunisian population: clinical investigation, molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulation of beta-catenin/E-cadherin complex.
authors: Kharrat, Marwa; Bouchaala, Wafa; Mohammed, Magdy M D; Issa, Abir Ben; Fakhfakh, Faiza; Kamoun, Fatma; Triki, Chahnez
one_liner_zh: 该文报道突尼斯CTNNB1综合征患者，用分子对接和MD模拟分析β-catenin/E-cadherin复合物突变影响，属蛋白-蛋白互作而非TF-DNA，但MD方法可迁移至蛋白-DNA互作研究。
abstract: BACKGROUND: CTNNB1 syndrome is a rare disorder caused by pathogenic variants of CTNNB1 gene, resulting in intellectual disability, peripheral spasticity, cognitive and motor impairments. The CTNNB1 encodes the beta-catenin protein, which plays dual roles in cells by forming synaptic adhesion through the E-cadherin/catenin adhesion complex and the activation of the Wnt signaling pathway. METHODS AND RESULTS: In this study, we describe for the first time a CTNNB1 syndrome in Tunisian children, by the description of two unrelated Tunisian patients with spastic paraplegia, intellectual disability and visual defect using whole exome sequencing. We identified a de novo nonsense (c.999 C > A; p.Tyr333X) mutation and a novel de novo frameshift variant (c.1041-1044 del; p.Val349Alafs*9) in the CTNNB1 gene, which were predicted to be pathogenic using in silico investigations. The identified (c.1041-1044 del) would lead to a frameshift followed by a premature stop codon, generating a nonsense mRNA that would probably escape nonsense-mediated decay. Thus, the nonsense mRNA could result in the premature translation termination and synthesis of dysfunctional protein with largely truncated ARM domains. The consequences of CTNNB1 frameshift variant were further explored together with wildtype through molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulations, which uncovered the disruption of beta-catenin function and the loss of its interacting counterparts. Hence, molecular dynamics simulation provides a comprehensive understanding of the conformational changes, compactness, folding and stability of the mutated beta-catenin protein. CONCLUSIONS: We present the first description of CTNNB1 syndrome in the Tunisian population and provide new insights into the usefulness of computational approaches to enlighten the molecular consequences of the frameshift variant p.Val349Alafs*9.
abstract_zh: 背景：CTNNB1综合征是一种由CTNNB1基因致病性变异引起的罕见疾病，导致智力障碍、外周痉挛、认知和运动功能障碍。CTNNB1编码β-连环蛋白（beta-catenin），该蛋白在细胞中具有双重作用，通过E-钙黏蛋白/连环蛋白黏附复合物形成突触黏附，并激活Wnt信号通路。方法与结果：在本研究中，我们首次描述了突尼斯儿童中的CTNNB1综合征，通过全外显子测序对两名无关的突尼斯患者进行描述，这些患者表现为痉挛性截瘫、智力障碍和视觉缺陷。我们在CTNNB1基因中鉴定出一个新生无义突变（c.999 C > A; p.Tyr333X）和一个新的新生移码变异（c.1041-1044 del; p.Val349Alafs*9），并通过计算机模拟预测其具有致病性。鉴定的（c.1041-1044 del）将导致移码并随后产生提前终止密码子，生成可能逃避无义介导衰变的无义mRNA。因此，该无义mRNA可能导致提前翻译终止，并合成具有大幅截短ARM结构域的功能异常蛋白。CTNNB1移码变异的后果进一步与野生型通过分子对接和分子动力学模拟进行探索，揭示了β-连环蛋白功能的破坏及其相互作用伙伴的丧失。因此，分子动力学模拟提供了对突变β-连环蛋白构象变化、紧凑性、折叠和稳定性的全面理解。结论：我们首次描述了突尼斯人群中的CTNNB1综合征，并为计算方法在阐明移码变异p.Val349Alafs*9分子后果方面的实用性提供了新见解。
